subject: 28 of 46 - and six instruments in one day that each measured something adjacent to what they claimed
body:
Ninth version, and the last of this stretch. Two more criteria decided, and a story about
my own tooling that I think is the most useful thing in it.

WHERE THE BOARD IS. This morning: 16 criteria automated against a denominator I had misremembered
as 40, 7 of them MET. Now: 28 of the spec's real 46 automated, 11 MET, 12 NOT MET, 5 ambiguous.

TODAY'S TWO:

C1.1 (one authoritative score function) -- NOT MET. Three independent score formulas remain:
CalculateScoreWithWeights, CalculateScoreWithWeightsEx, CalculateUnifiedScoreFromComponents. One
thing worth knowing: your 875-line CalculateEnhancedUnifiedScore is NOT one of them -- it calls
CalculateScoreWithWeights, so the small function is the root and the big one is a wrapper. The six
COMPONENT functions are properly unified; it is the combining step that still exists in three
copies.

C1.2 (one authoritative regime classifier) -- NOT MET, but only half of it. The structure is clean:
ClassifyBarToRegime is the single implementation, and both other entry points reach it. What is
missing is the declaration the criterion also asks for -- which entry point a given path should
use. That is a comment block, not a refactor. It is the cheapest remaining criterion on the board
by a wide margin.

NOW THE PART WORTH READING.

That checker's own documentation opens by warning that reading a passing test as evidence for a
criterion it does not address is the error that gave C6.1 a false pass this week. Its first run
then committed two errors of exactly that kind:

  It defined "score function" as "calls at least four component functions", which swept in six
  measurement and calibration routines that call components to MEASURE rather than to produce a
  score. It reported seven independent score implementations where there are three.

  It tested "precedence declared per path" by searching the whole file for the words "precedence"
  and "regime" -- and passed, on a comment about C operator precedence thirty thousand lines away
  from any classifier. C1.2 briefly read MET on that basis.

Both caught before the numbers reached you. But look at the day as a whole:

    five scripts published single points where the rule demanded curves
    the board hardcoded the criterion count it was built to stop me remembering
    the deflation record froze the numbers it was supposed to track
    the threshold audit called adaptation steps thresholds
    the sizing checker double-counted and blamed the wrong line
    this one passed on an unrelated comment

Six instruments, six defects of the same species: each measured something ADJACENT to what it
claimed. That is not carelessness I can fix by being more careful, and I have stopped treating it
that way. The one real fix I made today was making a whole class of it impossible -- results now go
through a writer that refuses to publish a malformed one and names the bad node. Everything else
was symptom repair.

STILL OPEN AND WAITING ON YOU: the two risk floors from the last version (0.5% hardcoded vs your
1.5% MinRiskPercent input). Nothing depends on it tonight, but it is a one-word change once you
say which you meant.

Run 5 is still calibrating.
